column1: high-key|/ˈhaɪ kiː/|CASUAL|B2|Openly, enthusiastically, or unmistakably feeling something.|Opposite of low-key; signals strong personal emphasis among friends.|I am high-key obsessed with the cold brew at that new corner cafe.|openly,totally,genuinely~subtly,secretly

vibe check|/vaɪb tʃɛk/|CASUAL|B2|A quick read of someone's mood or the atmosphere of a place.|Playful modern slang used before committing to a hangout.|Let's do a quick vibe check before we invite the whole floor to happy hour.|mood check,pulse check~obliviousness

legit|/ləˈdʒɪt/|CASUAL|B2|Genuine, impressive, or completely truthful.|Short for legitimate; doubles as an intensifier meaning genuinely.|Their rooftop tacos are legit the best thing I have eaten all month.|authentic,solid,genuinely~sketchy,fake

sketchy|/ˈskɛtʃi/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Suspicious, unsafe, or questionable in reliability.|Commonly describes neighborhoods, deals, or vague explanations.|That resale ticket site looks pretty sketchy, so let's buy directly from the venue.|shady,dubious,dicey~trustworthy,reputable

shady|/ˈʃeɪdi/|CASUAL|B2|Dishonest, sneaky, or subtly disrespectful.|Used for unethical business practices as well as passive-aggressive behavior.|Changing the contract terms right before signing felt really shady.|underhanded,sneaky~transparent,upfront

salty|/ˈsɔːlti/|CASUAL|B2|Bitter, resentful, or mildly upset over a minor setback.|Lighter than furious; often used teasingly among peers.|He is still salty about losing the trivia tiebreaker last night.|bitter,resentful,petty~gracious,unbothered

petty|/ˈpɛti/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Fixated on trivial grudges or minor score-settling.|Frequently used playfully to call out small acts of revenge.|Leaving him off the lunch order over one comment is honestly pretty petty.|spiteful,small-minded~magnanimous,generous

extra|/ˈɛkstrə/|CASUAL|B2|Over-the-top, dramatic, or needlessly elaborate.|Can be teasingly affectionate or mildly critical depending on tone.|Bringing a velvet pillow on a two-hour flight is a little extra.|dramatic,excessive~understated,minimal

bougie|/ˈbuːʒi/|CASUAL|C1|Tastefully upscale, pricey, or aspirationally luxurious.|Derived from bourgeois; often used humorously about everyday indulgences.|Spending nine dollars on artisanal toast feels gloriously bougie.|upscale,swanky,posh~no-frills,modest

chill|/tʃɪl/|CASUAL|B2|Relaxed, easygoing, or calmly unbothered.|Ubiquitous American marker of low-stress attitude or casual plans.|Do not stress about the dress code; the dinner is super chill.|laid-back,mellow,relaxed~uptight,tense

flaky|/ˈfleɪki/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Unreliable and prone to canceling plans at the last minute.|Focused on broken commitments rather than malice.|I love catching up with Sam, though he can be flaky on weeknights.|unreliable,inconsistent~dependable,punctual

bail (on)|/beɪl/|CASUAL|B2|Cancel plans or leave abruptly, often leaving others hanging.|Informal verb; pair with 'on' before a person or event.|Please do not bail on movie night after I already booked our seats.|cancel,flake out,ditch~show up,commit

ditch|/dɪtʃ/|CASUAL|B2|Abandon a plan, obligation, or person without much ceremony.|Stronger and blunter than skip; common in casual storytelling.|We decided to ditch the tourist bus and walk along the waterfront instead.|abandon,skip,drop~stick with,attend

bounce|/baʊns/|CASUAL|B2|Leave a gathering or location promptly.|Friendly, upbeat exit phrase common among younger professionals.|It is getting late, so I am going to bounce before the subway slows down.|head out,take off,split~hang around,stay

crash|/kræʃ/|CASUAL|B2|Sleep over informally or fall asleep quickly from exhaustion.|Also means showing up uninvited to a party.|You are welcome to crash on our guest sofa if the storm delays your train.|stay over,pass out~check in,stay awake

hang tight|/hæŋ taɪt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Wait patiently for a short time while something is arranged.|Reassuring and warm; natural in spoken American English and texts.|Hang tight for five minutes while I grab the parking pass from reception.|hold on,sit tight~rush ahead,leave

sit tight|/sɪt taɪt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Stay put and take no action until further notice.|Slightly calmer and more strategic than hang tight.|Sit tight until the recruiter sends the updated offer details.|wait patiently,hold steady~act hastily

my bad|/maɪ bæd/|CASUAL|B2|A brief, informal admission of a minor mistake.|Too casual for formal apologies; ideal for everyday slip-ups.|My bad—I attached last quarter's slide deck instead of the final version.|my mistake,oops,sorry~not my fault

fair enough|/fɛər ɪˈnʌf/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|A polite acknowledgment that someone's point or choice makes sense.|Signals gracious agreement even when you initially hoped otherwise.|You want to rest before tomorrow's flight? Fair enough, let's reschedule.|makes sense,valid point~unreasonable

no worries|/noʊ ˈwɜːriz/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|A relaxed way to say don't apologize or you're welcome.|Standard friendly American response that keeps the tone light.|No worries about the late reply; I just wrapped up my calls anyway.|don't sweat it,all good~big deal

don't sweat it|/doʊnt swɛt ɪt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Do not worry or stress about a minor problem.|Warm, encouraging reassurance when someone feels apologetic.|If the coffee spilled on the scratch notes, don't sweat it—I have backups.|relax,no biggie~worry about it

no biggie|/noʊ ˈbɪɡi/|CASUAL|B2|Not a major issue or inconvenience.|Short for no big deal; strictly informal.|Forgot the reusable bags? No biggie, we can grab paper ones.|no problem,minor issue~major setback

for real|/fɔːr riːl/|CASUAL|B2|Seriously, genuinely, or expressing disbelief.|Can be a question ('For real?') or an emphatic statement.|For real, that street violinist sounded like a conservatory soloist.|seriously,honestly,truly~jokingly,sarcastically

dead serious|/dɛd ˈsɪriəs/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Completely earnest with zero humor or exaggeration.|Used to stop someone from assuming you are joking.|I am dead serious—we can hike the whole ridge before noon.|completely earnest,not joking~kidding,teasing

spot on|/spɑːt ɑːn/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Exactly right or remarkably accurate.|Originally British, now widely embraced in US conversation and media.|Your prediction about the commuter traffic was spot on.|dead-on,accurate,exact~off base,inaccurate

dead-on|/dɛd ɑːn/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Precisely accurate in aim, judgment, or impersonation.|Punchier American variant of spot on.|Her impression of our neighborhood barista was dead-on.|exact,spot on,uncanny~way off,wrong

off base|/ɔːf beɪs/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Mistaken, inaccurate, or out of line in an assumption.|Baseball metaphor implying a runner caught away from safety.|Tell me if I am off base, but it seems like the timeline is too tight.|mistaken,misguided~accurate,on target

way off|/weɪ ɔːf/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Far from the true figure, target, or interpretation.|Natural everyday way to flag a large discrepancy.|My estimate for the grocery bill was way off this week.|far off,inaccurate~close,accurate

on point|/ɑːn pɔɪnt/|CASUAL|B2|Sharp, stylish, or executed with impressive precision.|Complimentary slang covering outfits, timing, and arguments.|Your timing with the dessert order was absolutely on point.|sharp,impeccable,nailed it~sloppy,off

nailed it|/neɪld ɪt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Executed something flawlessly on the first or decisive try.|Upbeat praise used after talks, performances, or tricky tasks.|You nailed it in that client Q&A—every answer sounded effortless.|crushed it,aced it~botched it,bombed

crushed it|/krʌʃt ɪt/|CASUAL|B2|Performed remarkably well and exceeded expectations.|High-energy American encouragement common in gyms, startups, and friendships.|You totally crushed it during your first half-marathon.|killed it,dominated~struggled,flubbed

bombed|/bɑːmd/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Failed badly, especially in a public performance or exam.|Common in stand-up comedy, interviews, and test recaps.|I thought I bombed the oral interview, yet they invited me to the final round.|flopped,tanked~aced,succeeded

tanked|/tæŋkt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Dropped sharply in value, quality, or performance.|Frequently used for exams, box-office numbers, and stocks.|Our quiz average tanked after everyone skipped the idiom review.|plummeted,crashed,flopped~soared,spiked

flubbed|/flʌbd/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Botched a line, catch, or small action awkwardly.|Lighter and less catastrophic than bombed.|I flubbed the host's last name on the first take, so we recorded it again.|fumbled,botched,messed up~executed smoothly

botched|/bɑːtʃt/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Ruined through carelessness or poor execution.|Often applies to repairs, plans, or announcements.|The contractor botched the tile grout and had to redo the whole shower.|bungled,mishandled~mastered,perfected

clueless|/ˈkluːləs/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Completely unaware or lacking basic knowledge about something.|Direct informal adjective; soften if speaking about colleagues.|I was totally clueless about local parking rules during my first week in Chicago.|oblivious,uninformed~savvy,informed

savvy|/ˈsævi/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Shrewd, practical, and well-informed in a given domain.|High-praise word common in both casual and professional American speech.|She is remarkably tech-savvy and fixed the router in two minutes.|astute,sharp,street-smart~naive,clueless

street-smart|/striːt smɑːrt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Possessing practical survival sense gained from real-world experience.|Contrasts with purely academic 'book-smart' knowledge.|Growing up in New York made him street-smart about spotting tourist traps.|shrewd,resourceful~naive,sheltered

amped|/æmpt/|CASUAL|B2|Excited, energized, and eager for something to begin.|Short for amplified; popular in sports and concert settings.|Everyone is amped for the outdoor jazz festival this Saturday.|pumped,hyped,stoked~drained,indifferent

stoked|/stoʊkt/|CASUAL|B2|Thrilled and enthusiastically happy about good news.|Originally California surf slang, now nationwide American English.|We are stoked that you finally got approved for the apartment.|thrilled,ecstatic,pumped~bummed,underwhelmed

bummed|/bʌmd/|CASUAL|B2|Disappointed or mildly downcast.|Soft everyday word for minor letdowns rather than deep grief.|I am really bummed that the coastal trail closed for maintenance.|disappointed,let down~thrilled,stoked

psyched|/saɪkt/|CASUAL|B2|Mentally energized and eagerly looking forward to an event.|Common across generations in casual American speech.|I am psyched to try out the pottery studio next Thursday.|excited,eager,pumped~dreading,unenthused

wired|/waɪərd/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Overstimulated with nervous energy, often from caffeine or adrenaline.|Usually implies difficulty winding down or sleeping.|After two afternoon espressos, I am way too wired to nap.|jittery,buzzing,hyper~drowsy,mellow

zonked|/zɑːŋkt/|CASUAL|C1|Completely exhausted and ready to fall asleep immediately.|Playful, expressive slang after a long day or travel.|After a red-eye flight across three time zones, I was totally zonked.|wiped out,spent,exhausted~energized,refreshed

wiped out|/waɪpt aʊt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Physically or mentally drained of energy.|Also means financially ruined or crashing on a surfboard.|Moving boxes up four flights of stairs left all of us wiped out.|exhausted,beat,drained~recharged,rested

beat|/biːt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Very tired after a long stretch of effort.|Short, classic American adjective used predicatively ('I'm beat').|Let's order takeout tonight—I am completely beat after that double shift.|exhausted,worn out~energetic,fresh

hangry|/ˈhæŋɡri/|CASUAL|B2|Irritable or short-tempered specifically because of hunger.|Blend of hungry and angry; widely used with humor.|Let's grab a quick sandwich before everyone gets hangry on the road trip.|cranky,famished~satiated,content

famished|/ˈfæmɪʃt/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Extremely hungry, often stated with playful exaggeration.|Slightly more elevated than starving while still conversational.|After swimming laps for an hour, I am absolutely famished.|starving,ravenous~stuffed,full

stuffed|/stʌft/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Uncomfortably or completely full after eating.|Everyday American alternative to 'overly satiated'.|Thanks for offering pie, but I am totally stuffed from dinner.|full,satiated~hungry,famished

grub|/ɡrʌb/|CASUAL|B2|Informal food or a casual meal.|Warm, down-to-earth slang used for diners, tacos, or snacks.|Let's go grab some quick grub near the ballpark before first pitch.|food,eats,bites~fine dining

craving|/ˈkreɪvɪŋ/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|A sudden, strong desire for a specific food or experience.|Common both as a verb and noun in everyday chat.|I have been craving hot ramen ever since the temperature dropped.|hankering,urge,desire~aversion,indifference

hit the spot|/hɪt ðə spɑːt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Satisfy a craving or physical need completely.|Classic American compliment for food, drinks, or a hot shower.|That cold lemonade really hit the spot after mowing the lawn.|satisfy,do the trick~fall flat,disappoint

do the trick|/duː ðə trɪk/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Solve a problem or achieve the desired effect simply.|Practical everyday expression for fixes and remedies.|A drop of oil on the squeaky hinge should do the trick.|work,suffice,solve it~fail,fall short

game-changer|/ˈɡeɪm ˌtʃeɪndʒər/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|A discovery, habit, or tool that dramatically improves a situation.|Used enthusiastically for both consumer products and major strategies.|Switching to a standing desk was a total game-changer for my back.|breakthrough,revelation~minor tweak

lifesaver|/ˈlaɪfˌseɪvər/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Someone or something that rescues you from a stressful jam.|Warm expression of gratitude in everyday speech.|Bringing a spare phone charger to the airport made you a total lifesaver.|hero,godsend,rescue~hindrance

clutch|/klʌtʃ/|CASUAL|C1|Dependable or lifesaving precisely in a high-pressure moment.|Sports-derived slang now used for friends, snacks, and timely help.|Her umbrella was so clutch when the downpour started right after work.|crucial,timely,lifesaving~unhelpful,late

go-to|/ˈɡoʊ tuː/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|The default, most trusted choice you rely on repeatedly.|Works as a noun or adjective for restaurants, songs, or contacts.|Thai basil fried rice is my go-to weeknight takeout order.|default,staple,favorite~last resort

must-have|/mʌst hæv/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|An essential item or feature considered indispensable.|Common in shopping, travel packing, and product advice.|A lightweight rain shell is a must-have if you visit Seattle in April.|essential,staple~optional,luxury

dealbreaker|/ˈdiːlˌbreɪkər/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|A single flaw or condition that immediately ends your interest.|Used in apartment hunting, dating, and contract negotiations.|Having no in-unit laundry was a dealbreaker for our apartment search.|non-starter,showstopper~minor flaw

non-starter|/nɑːn ˈstɑːrtər/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|An idea or proposal impossible to consider seriously from the start.|Polite yet firm way to reject unworkable suggestions.|A two-hour daily commute is a non-starter for me right now.|unworkable,dead end~viable option

showstopper|/ˈʃoʊˌstɑːpər/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Either a dazzling highlight or a critical bug that halts progress.|Context signals whether it means crowd-pleaser or major blocker.|The homemade mango tart was the absolute showstopper of the dinner party.|standout,highlight,blocker~forgettable

crowd-pleaser|/kraʊd ˈpliːzər/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Something reliably enjoyed by almost everyone in a group.|Popular for recipes, movies, and playlist picks.|Baked mac and cheese is always a safe crowd-pleaser at potlucks.|fan favorite,sure hit~polarizing pick

hit or miss|/hɪt ɔːr mɪs/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Inconsistent—sometimes great and sometimes disappointing.|Honest everyday review phrase for cafes, weather, or sequels.|The service at that diner is hit or miss, though the pancakes are great.|uneven,inconsistent~reliable,consistent

so-so|/ˈsoʊ soʊ/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Average, unremarkable, and neither good nor terrible.|Often paired with a flat hand-wobble gesture in American speech.|The movie looked stunning, but the plot was just so-so.|mediocre,middling,meh~outstanding,awful

meh|/mɛ/|CASUAL|B2|Indifferent, unimpressed, or mildly underwhelming.|Interjection and adjective capturing total lack of excitement.|I tried the viral matcha latte and honestly felt pretty meh about it.|underwhelming,so-so~amazing,thrilling

overrated|/ˌoʊvərˈreɪtɪd/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Praised far more enthusiastically than its real quality deserves.|Frequently sparks friendly debates about films, cities, or trends.|Honestly, waiting two hours for brunch on Sunday is wildly overrated.|overhyped,exaggerated~underrated,essential

underrated|/ˌʌndərˈreɪtɪd/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Better or more valuable than most people give it credit for.|Common way to champion hidden gems or quiet habits.|Taking a twenty-minute walk without headphones is seriously underrated.|underappreciated,hidden gem~overhyped,overrated

overhyped|/ˌoʊvərˈhaɪpt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Promoted with excessive buzz that outpaces reality.|Especially common for tech launches, restaurants, and blockbusters.|The pop-up dessert bar was overhyped and way too crowded.|overblown,overrated~understated,genuine

hyped|/haɪpt/|CASUAL|B2|Very excited or heavily promoted with enthusiastic buzz.|Pairs naturally with 'up' or 'for' in casual conversation.|We are so hyped for the championship game this weekend.|pumped,thrilled,stoked~bored,indifferent

slept on|/slɛpt ɑːn/|CASUAL|C1|Unfairly overlooked or ignored despite high quality.|Past-participle slang from music and sports culture.|That tiny Ethiopian bakery on Fourth Street is seriously slept on.|overlooked,underrated~hyped,mainstream

fire|/faɪər/|CASUAL|B2|Exceptionally good, stylish, or exciting.|Slang adjective used predicatively ('That playlist is fire').|The acoustic live version of that track is pure fire.|incredible,top-notch,lit~weak,boring

solid|/ˈsɑːlɪd/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Dependably good, well-crafted, or trustworthy.|Understated praise widely used in American conversation and work.|That was a solid presentation—clear numbers and zero fluff.|dependable,strong,good~flimsy,weak

top-notch|/tɑːp nɑːtʃ/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Of the very highest quality or standard.|Warm, universally polite praise across age groups.|The customer support team at that local bike shop is top-notch.|first-rate,superb,stellar~subpar,mediocre

stellar|/ˈstɛlər/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Outstanding or impressively well executed.|Upbeat compliment usable in both social and workplace chats.|You did a stellar job organizing the neighborhood block party.|superb,exceptional~mediocre,poor

subpar|/sʌbˈpɑːr/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Below the expected standard of quality.|Golf-derived word that sounds polite yet crisp.|The hotel wifi was subpar for anyone trying to take video calls.|below average,mediocre~top-notch,superior

janky|/ˈdʒæŋki/|CASUAL|C1|Poorly constructed, glitchy, or awkwardly rigged together.|Popular in tech, DIY, and everyday complaints about cheap gear.|The old tripod is a little janky, so tape the leg before filming.|rickety,glitchy,shoddy~sturdy,polished

wonky|/ˈwɑːŋki/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Crooked, behaving strangely, or slightly out of alignment.|Friendly, mild word for tech glitches or wobbly furniture.|My laptop trackpad has been acting wonky since the last update.|glitchy,unsteady,quirky~smooth,steady

glitchy|/ˈɡlɪtʃi/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Prone to brief technical errors, freezes, or erratic behavior.|Standard modern word for apps, livestreams, and audio.|The transit app gets glitchy whenever it rains heavily.|buggy,wonky,unstable~seamless,smooth

clunky|/ˈklʌŋki/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Awkward, bulky, or needlessly complicated to use.|Applies equally to software interfaces, phrasing, and shoes.|The registration form felt clunky on a phone screen.|awkward,cumbersome~sleek,intuitive

sleek|/sliːk/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Smooth, streamlined, and effortlessly stylish.|Compliment for product design, interfaces, and architecture.|The redesigned library app looks super sleek and easy to scan.|streamlined,polished~clunky,bulky

snazzy|/ˈsnæzi/|CASUAL|C1|Flashy, smartly styled, or eye-catching in a fun way.|Playful compliment for outfits, sneakers, or gadgets.|Look at those snazzy new sneakers—are you running a race later?|stylish,sharp,spiffy~drab,plain

spiffy|/ˈspɪfi/|CASUAL|C1|Neatly dressed, tidy, or freshly spruced up.|Lighthearted, affectionate American slang with vintage charm.|You look pretty spiffy in that linen blazer today.|sharp,dapper,neat~scruffy,rumpled

scruffy|/ˈskrʌfi/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Untidy, slightly worn, or casually unshaven.|Can be affectionate for pets or mildly critical for attire.|I feel a bit scruffy showing up to a gallery opening in hiking boots.|unkempt,rumpled,shabby~polished,spiffy

cheesy|/ˈtʃiːzi/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Overly sentimental, corny, or lacking subtlety.|Frequently said with fond self-awareness about rom-coms or puns.|I know it sounds cheesy, but watching the sunrise together never gets old.|corny,sappy,tacky~subtle,sophisticated

corny|/ˈkɔːrni/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Predictably old-fashioned, trite, or dad-joke level humorous.|Classic American term for overly earnest jokes or clichés.|His pun about the bakery was painfully corny, yet everyone laughed.|cheesy,trite,cringey~witty,fresh

cringe|/krɪndʒ/|CASUAL|B2|Awkwardly embarrassing to watch or remember.|Used as both a verb and an informal adjective.|Reading my college blog posts ten years later makes me cringe.|awkward,embarrassing~cool,graceful

awkward|/ˈɔːkwərd/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Socially uncomfortable, clumsy, or hard to navigate.|One of the most frequent American words for minor social friction.|There was an awkward five-second pause when we both reached for the check.|uncomfortable,clumsy~smooth,effortless

vibe|/vaɪb/|CASUAL|B2|The unspoken emotional tone or aesthetic feel of a person or place.|Flexible noun and verb ('vibing with') in everyday US English.|This bookstore cafe has such a warm, quiet Sunday vibe.|atmosphere,energy,feel~tension,clash

click (with)|/klɪk/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Immediately bond or get along effortlessly with someone.|Also means suddenly understanding a tricky concept.|We clicked within five minutes of talking about vintage cameras.|hit it off,bond,mesh~clash,butt heads

hit it off|/hɪt ɪt ɔːf/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Develop quick, natural rapport upon first meeting.|Friendly, universal phrase for friendships, dates, or teammates.|The new designer and our engineering lead hit it off right away.|click,bond quickly~clash,alienate

mesh (with)|/mɛʃ/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Blend harmoniously with a group, schedule, or style.|Mechanical gear metaphor applied smoothly to people and plans.|Her relaxed travel pace meshed perfectly with ours in Lisbon.|gel,align,blend~clash,conflict

gel (with)|/dʒɛl/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Come together smoothly as a team, plan, or friendship.|Implies cohesion forming over time rather than instantly.|It took two weeks for the new bandmates to really gel on stage.|bond,cohere,mesh~fragment,clash

butt heads|/bʌt hɛdz/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Argue stubbornly or collide over strong differing opinions.|Evokes two rams locking horns; common for family or coworkers.|They used to butt heads over editing style, though now they respect each other.|clash,quarrel,disagree~see eye to eye,agree

in sync|/ɪn sɪŋk/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Coordinated smoothly in timing, rhythm, or thinking.|Short for synchronized; works for schedules, teams, and tastes.|After cooking together for years, they move completely in sync in the kitchen.|coordinated,aligned~out of sync,mismatched

out of the loop|/aʊt əv ðə luːp/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Uninformed about recent news, gossip, or ongoing decisions.|Contrasts directly with 'in the loop'.|Sorry I missed the joke—I have been out of the loop all week on vacation.|uninformed,clueless~in the know,updated

in the know|/ɪn ðə noʊ/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Privately informed about insider details or upcoming trends.|Lightly conspiratorial or admiring tone.|Locals in the know order the off-menu spicy dumplings before noon.|informed,plugged in~out of the loop

plugged in|/plʌɡd ɪn/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Well connected and actively up to date on news or community trends.|Modern metaphor implying steady connection to a network.|Maya is super plugged in to the Austin indie film scene.|connected,informed~disconnected,out of touch

out of touch|/aʊt əv tʌtʃ/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|No longer aware of current realities, prices, or feelings.|Can mean losing contact with a friend or lacking modern perspective.|Anyone thinking rent still costs half that is seriously out of touch.|disconnected,oblivious~in tune,plugged in

tight (with)|/taɪt/|CASUAL|B2|Very close and loyal as friends.|Short, warm slang adjective ('We've been tight since high school').|Sam and Devon have been super tight since they shared a tiny dorm.|close,inseparable~distant,estranged

go way back|/ɡoʊ weɪ bæk/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Have known someone for many years.|Friendly way to explain instant trust or shared history.|Elena and my brother go way back—they played soccer together at age ten.|have history,be old friends~just met

wingman|/ˈwɪŋmæn/|CASUAL|C1|A supportive friend who backs you up in a social situation.|Aviation term adopted into everyday social slang.|Thanks for being my wingman at the networking mixer tonight.|sidekick,ally,backup~rival

vouch for|/vaʊtʃ fɔːr/|CONVERSATIONAL|C1|Personally guarantee someone's character, skill, or honesty.|Carries genuine personal credibility.|I worked beside Priya for three years and can vouch for her reliability.|endorse,attest to~doubt,discredit

props|/prɑːps/|CASUAL|B2|Well-earned respect, credit, or praise.|Short for 'proper respect'; usually paired with 'give' or 'mad'.|Major props to Leo for fixing the leaky sink before guests arrived.|kudos,credit,respect~criticism,shade

kudos|/ˈkuːdoʊz/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|Friendly public praise or congratulations for an achievement.|Common in Slack channels, emails, and casual conversation.|Kudos to everyone who helped set up the charity book drive.|praise,props,applause~blame,criticism

shout-out|/ˈʃaʊt aʊt/|CONVERSATIONAL|B2|A public thank-you or appreciative mention of someone.|Originally hip-hop radio slang, now mainstream even in town halls.|Quick shout-out to Jordan for bringing fresh bagels for the morning shift.|mention,nod,thank-you~snub,oversight

hype someone up|/haɪp ˈsʌmwʌn ʌp/|CASUAL|B2|Cheer someone on enthusiastically to boost their confidence.|Warm, supportive friend-group slang.|My sister always calls ten minutes before an interview to hype me up.|cheer on,pump up~discourage,deflate

gas someone up|/ɡæs ˈsʌmwʌn ʌp/|CASUAL|C1|Flatter or enthusiastically boost someone's ego or excitement.|Usually affectionate among friends, occasionally implies over-flattery.|Everyone in the group chat gassed him up after he posted his marathon finish.|flatter,hype up~put down,humble
